defs_parts: Five labels sit in the corners of the pictures that follow.
Video only: the term comes from a video lecture, and is not in the course text or on the term list.
Computed: the numbers are worked out on screen from stated inputs.
Simulation: a model run step by step from stated rules, not a measurement of a real game.
Illustrative data: numbers chosen to show the idea, not measured.
Conceptual: a drawing of the idea, with no data behind it.
recap_lines: Descriptive play shows a response, and evaluative play asks why it matters.
Risk versus reward pays more for the harder, riskier action.
A trade-off is one swap, and persistence makes a choice stick for a set time.
Situational choice depends on the moment, personalisation on the player's style.
Difficulty is how hard it is, and fairness is whether you can learn from losing.
Rock-paper-scissors keeps options balanced, and short turns keep downtime low.
bookends.command: Quiz me on game design terms with short game-making cases, one at a time. Use descriptive play, evaluative play, agency, risk versus reward, trade-off, persistence, situational choice, personalisation, difficulty and fairness. For each case I must name the exact term and say why its look-alike is wrong. Hold back the answer until I reply, then tell me if I was right.
checks: Check: each case is a game-making situation, and the answer waits for you.
Check: you named the exact term and said why its look-alike is wrong.
